item.title: Propose a second life for discarded costumes
item.context_text: A local theatre clears costumes after a production. One school wants whole costumes, while a repair class wants material from damaged pieces.
item.objective_text: Sort the offer by condition, record a fair response deadline, and avoid promising duplicates.
success_conditions: Sort the offer by condition, record a fair response deadline, and avoid promising duplicates.
List faults for the repair class

children.title: Read the stock list
children.instructions: Read closely and use the details to answer.
children.prompt_text: There are eight wearable coats, two coats with broken fastenings, and six damaged canvas aprons. The school asks for six wearable coats. The sewing class accepts items that can be taken apart. The theatre can store everything for two more weeks.

questions.prompt: Which items could fill the school’s request straight away?
options: The two coats with broken fastenings
questions.explanation: The school requested wearable coats and eight are available.

questions.prompt: Which claim about storage is supported?
options: The theatre will store them indefinitely
Everything has to be removed today
Materials can remain there for two weeks
questions.explanation: The stock list gives a two-week window.

children.title: Hear the wardrobe manager
children.instructions: Listen twice. First identify the update, then check the details you need.
children.prompt_text: Two of the wearable coats actually match a complete set, and an amateur group might need it. We can offer six other wearable coats to the school first. Keep matching pieces together for one week. Offer damaged aprons and coats to the repair class now, but list the faults.

questions.prompt: How many wearable coats can the school get without breaking the set?
questions.explanation: The eight wearable items include two matching ones, leaving six.

questions.prompt: What information do repair learners need before accepting the donations?
options: What the school plans to do
Which items have faults and what they are
questions.explanation: The manager asks for a fault list so the class can judge whether it can use the items.

children.title: Respond to the teacher by phone
children.prompt_text: The teacher asks whether all eight coats can be reserved immediately.
children.instructions: Explain what can be promised, why the other coats are temporarily separate and when you can give a final answer.
children.goal: Give an actionable response to what you just learned.
children.model_answer: We can reserve six wearable coats today. The other two form a matching set, and we are holding them together for a week. I’ll confirm after that whether the set is still available. I can email the confirmed allocation today.

children.title: Send the sorting plan to volunteers
children.prompt_text: The volunteer team collects the items next Tuesday.
children.instructions: Write a practical inventory note. State the current destinations, the condition information to record, and what to do if nobody takes the set before storage ends.
children.goal: Sort the offer by condition, record a fair response deadline, and avoid promising duplicates.
children.model_answer: Mark six wearable coats for the school and keep the matching set of two on hold until next Tuesday. Offer both coats with broken fastenings and the six damaged canvas aprons to the sewing class, with a note about each fault. If the matching set is released and still unclaimed near the two-week storage limit, offer it as a pair before arranging another destination with the theatre manager.
